Subject: Renewal uplift — mid-contract capacity increase and co-term timing

Hi Jamie / Linda,

Following up from last week's call — Polaris is forecasting a mid-contract uplift of ~45% in committed GPU hours starting June 1 to support the new patient inference pipeline. We ran the numbers on Redwood's side and put together two practical packaging paths so you can choose what fits procurement and exec priorities:

- Option A (Annualize + Co-term): Move uplift onto an annualized, co-termed contract (sync to existing Jan renewal) — 10% uplift discount if Polaris commits to annualized billing and co-term. Faster capacity SLA (guaranteed burst buffer) included.
- Option B (Short-term Topup): 6-month top-up addendum billed prorated; no co-term. Lower near-term commitment but higher unit price.

Attached is a one-pager with the economics and a simple mutual action timeline for legal and procurement. Quick asks from our side:
1) Which option best fits Polaris procurement and exec approval timeline?
2) Do you need an initial PO/advance to reserve the uplifted capacity?
3) Any required timing constraints for invoicing (monthly vs. upfront)?

Ben and Marissa are on this thread for pricing/legal coordination — Ben will outline exact dollar figures and Marissa will own the mutual action plan + SOW changes.

Thanks — happy to jump on a 30m call if that helps.

Best,
Sofia Ivanova
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Jamie / Linda — good to hear Option A is preferred. Below are three precise pricing constructs (rounded) so you can route to finance:

1) Annualized Co-term (preferred): add uplift as annualized capacity, alignment to Jan renewal.
   - Uplift volume: +45% (est. 16k GPU hours/month)
   - Effective unit rate (after 10% conditional discount): $0.0125 / GPU-hour
   - Annualized incremental spend: ~$72,000
   - Invoice timing: Annual upfront or quarterly installments (both supported)

2) 12-month Fixed Addendum (no co-term): same economics as above but 7.5% discount instead of 10%.

3) 6-month Top-up (short-term): prorated billing at $0.0148 / GPU-hour, no discount.

Notes:
- The 10% discount is conditional on: (a) co-term agreement and (b) commit to annualized billing OR a 6-month upfront deposit that covers the uplift.
- If Polaris requests a shorter commit but wants the 10% discount, we'll need an exec credit approval (sales + finance sign-off) — can be done but takes ~3 business days.

I've attached the spreadsheet with line items and invoice examples. If procurement favors net-30, the discount remains available but we'll need a signed amendment before capacity is reserved.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
